findings.evidence: Lines 52, 57, 322, and 361 impose `Field`, `Ring`/`CommRing`, and `FiniteDimensional`; Mathlib’s `TensorProduct.dualDistribEquiv` at `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Contraction.lean:456-463` requires only finite free modules over a commutative semiring, while `Bialgebra` and `HopfAlgebra` are defined over `CommSemiring`/`Semiring` in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Bialgebra/Basic.lean:57` and `Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/Basic.lean:65`.
findings.fix: Generalize the file to `[CommSemiring k] [Semiring H] [Bialgebra k H] [Module.Finite k H] [Module.Free k H]`, using `[CommSemiring H]` only for `instIsCocomm`; give the Hopf section the analogous semiring assumptions. At minimum, remove the unused `Ring`/`CommRing` strengthening.
findings.issue: All public structures are restricted to `[Field k] [Ring H] [FiniteDimensional k H]` (and cocommutativity to `CommRing H`), although the natural finite-dual construction works for a finite free bialgebra over a commutative semiring; this also stops short of the roadmap’s finite-locally-free base-ring setting.

summary: The construction is stated with substantially stronger scalar and algebra assumptions than the finite-free duality machinery requires.
